title: Game View & Play Mode
description: Configure resolution, aspect ratio, and learn every detail of Play mode testing.

slides.title: Game View Control Bar 🎮
slides.content:
# The Game View Toolbar

At the top of the Game view you’ll find:
- **Display**: Choose which camera to show (by default Display 1 uses the Main Camera).
- **Aspect Ratio / Resolution**: Pick a target resolution (e.g., 16:9, 1920×1080) or create a custom one.
- **Scale**: Zoom the rendered image (e.g., 1x, 2x) without changing resolution.
- **Maximize On Play**: When enabled, the Game view expands to full editor window on Play.
- **Stats**: Shows rendering statistics (FPS, batches, tris).
- **Gizmos**: Toggle to see gizmos (like colliders) in the Game view.

quizData.question: What does the 'Maximize On Play' button do?

options.text: It makes the Game view fullscreen when entering Play mode

quizData.explanation: Maximize On Play causes the Game view to take up the entire Editor window while playing.

slides.title: Play Mode Controls ▶️
slides.content:
# Play, Pause, Step

- **Play** (Ctrl+P / Cmd+P): Starts the game.
- **Pause**: Freezes the current frame. You can still modify values and see the effect.
- **Step**: Advances one frame while paused. Useful for debugging frame‑by‑frame.
- **Stop**: Exits Play mode and discards all runtime changes.

quizData.question: What happens to runtime modifications when you stop Play mode?

options.text: They are saved to the scene
They are written to a log file
They are automatically applied to prefabs

quizData.explanation: All changes made during Play mode are temporary and lost when you stop.

slides.title: Pro Tip 🚀
slides.content:
## Use the Stats Window

Enable **Stats** to monitor performance. Keep an eye on **SetPass calls** and **batches**; high numbers can indicate optimization needs.
